title: Dhruv and the North Star.
lines: This is a very old story from India.
Long ago there lived a king.
His name was Uttanapada.
He had two wives and two sons.
One son was called Uttam.
His mother was Queen Suruchi.
She was beautiful, but not always kind.
The other son was called Dhruv.
His mother was Suniti.
She was gentle and wise and kind.
The king loved Suruchi and her son Uttam the most.
Uttam was always allowed to sit on the king's lap.
One day little Dhruv saw that.
Dhruv was five years old.
He really wanted to sit on his daddy's lap too.
He walked to the throne and tried to climb onto the king's lap.
But Queen Suruchi stopped him.
No, she said sternly.
You can't sit here.
This place is for my son.
If you want to sit on the king's lap, you'll have to ask God to let you be my son in another life.
The king said nothing.
Dhruv felt very sad.
His heart hurt.
He ran crying to his mummy.
Suniti took him in her arms.
She wiped away his tears.
My dear Dhruv, she said.
Don't be angry with the queen.
Being angry makes your heart heavy.
But do you know what?
There is someone who loves everyone just the same.
Big or small, rich or poor.
That is God, Lord Vishnu.
If you really look for him with all your heart, he will find you.
Dhruv wiped his nose.
Then I'll go and look for him, he said.
And he walked away, into the big forest.
Dhruv was only five years old.
The forest was big and dark.
There were tigers and bears and snakes.
But Dhruv wasn't afraid.
In the forest he met a wise man.
The man had a long white beard and carried a lute.
It was the wise Narada.
Where are you going, little boy?
asked Narada.
I'm looking for Lord Vishnu, said Dhruv.
Narada smiled kindly.
That's very difficult, he said.
Grown men try their whole lives.
Go back home.
But Dhruv shook his head.
I'm not going back.
Narada saw that Dhruv meant it.
All right then, he said.
I'll teach you how to pray.
Sit down by the river.
Be very still.
Think only of Vishnu.
And repeat this little prayer.
He whispered a little prayer into Dhruv's ear.
Dhruv sat down by the river.
He closed his eyes.
He was very still.
He repeated the little prayer.
Day and night.
He ate only a little fruit, and later only leaves.
He thought only of Vishnu.
The wind blew.
The rain fell.
But Dhruv stayed sitting.
The animals of the forest came to look.
The tiger lay down next to him, very calmly.
The little birds sang for him.
Even the gods in the sky saw it.
How strong that little boy is!
they said.
After a long time Dhruv felt a warm light.
He opened his eyes.
There stood Lord Vishnu.
He was blue and shining.
He had four arms and he was smiling.
Dhruv, said Vishnu, you have looked for me with all your heart.
What do you wish for?
Dhruv looked at Vishnu.
Suddenly he didn't feel sad anymore.
No more anger.
His heart was full of light.
I don't wish for anything anymore, said Dhruv.
I have found you.
That is enough.
Vishnu was so happy with that answer.
You will go back to your daddy, he said.
And one day you'll be a good king.
But I'll give you something else.
When you are very old, you will become a star in the sky.
A star that never moves.
All the other stars will turn around you.
And sailors and travellers will look at you to find their way.
Dhruv went back home.
His daddy ran to him and took him in his arms.
I'm sorry, said the king.
I love you just as much.
Even Queen Suruchi said sorry.
And later Dhruv became a wise, good king.
And tonight, take a look at the sky.
There's a star that always stays in the same place, in the north.
In India they call that star Dhruv Tara.
Dhruv's star.
Here we call it the North Star.
The end.
